scope: N5.3 optional table/scenery reference records; not deployed Weapon/Equipment or Army carriers

records.name: Special Terrain
records.summary: Optional battlefield areas agreed before play, configured with a Terrain Type and at least one additional characteristic. Their boundaries and effects belong to the current game table, not an Army or Unit Profile.

effects: During game-table setup, both players agree on the location and characteristics of Special Terrain zones and mark boundaries clearly using scenery, templates, or other representations.

Every Special Terrain area has a Terrain Type: Aquatic, Desert, Mountain, Jungle, or Zero-G. The Type is chosen before Deployment and determines whether a Trooper's [[skill:terrain]] Special Skill is applicable.
Each Special Terrain area must also have at least one additional characteristic: Difficult Terrain, Saturation, or Visibility Conditions. These characteristics may be combined.
Special Terrain areas have infinite height unless otherwise specified.
A Trooper is affected while in Silhouette contact with the area or when its base or Silhouette Template is at least partly covered by the area.
restrictions: Special Terrain is optional and requires agreement between players before play.
The named examples in the Special Terrain suggestions table are illustrative combinations, not additional canonical Terrain Types or mandatory game-table elements.

records.name: Access Width
records.summary: Narrow and Wide scenery access points constrain passage by Silhouette, with an explicit [[state:prone|Prone]]/Silhouette X exception. Their gate Tokens label scenery openings, not deployed Weapons or Equipment.

effects: Players agree on the Access Width of scenery openings during table setup and mark each as a Narrow Gate or Wide Gate Token.
Narrow access points permit passage only to Troopers with a Silhouette Attribute of 2 or lower; Wide access points permit all Troopers regardless of Silhouette.
Access Width restrictions take priority over the General Movement Rules and the Requirements of Skills with the Movement Label. A Trooper lacking the required Silhouette cannot pass.
Gates and access points are treated as open and do not block Line of Fire unless a specific rule or scenario condition says otherwise.
restrictions: Troopers in [[state:prone|Prone State]] with Silhouette X use the Silhouette Attribute on their Unit Profile when checking access restrictions.
Access Width is a property of the agreed scenery layout, not an intrinsic permanent can-pass property of a Trooper. Gate Tokens are labels, not independently placed game devices.
